quandoUsar: Frequently asked questions on a pricing or help page, with `size="lg"` for questions in large text and answers in reading-size body text.
Supporting information that only some people need, such as billing or privacy details, without taking anyone off the page.
Lists where only one answer needs to stay open: opening an item closes the previous one, and clicking the open item closes it.
quandoEvitar: Use `bouncy-accordion` when you need several items open at the same time or controlled state; this accordion only has `defaultOpen`.
Use `collapsible` for a single region that opens and closes next to its own title.
Use `faq-section` when the page needs a whole section of questions, with topics or search.

teclado.acao: Opens the focused item and closes the one that was open; on an item that is already open, closes it.
Moves focus to the next or previous title, wrapping to the first after the last.
Moves focus to the first or last title.

acessibilidade: Built on the Radix Accordion: each title is a `<button>` inside an `<h3>`, with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`, and each panel is a `region` tied to its title.
When it finishes collapsing, the panel gets `visibility: hidden` and leaves the Tab order and the accessibility tree; the screen reader only finds the open answer.
The heading level is fixed at `<h3>`; if the page hierarchy calls for another level, use `bouncy-accordion`, which accepts `headingLevel`.
movimento: The panel height follows the content on a no-overshoot spring, and the answer moves down 6 px out of a slight blur as it appears.
The arrow rotates 180° on a short spring; switching items mid-animation redirects the height instead of restarting.
With “reduce motion” on, panels and arrow go straight to the final state, without animation.
responsivo: At size `lg`, below 520 px the minimum title height drops from 76 to 68 px and the fonts go down one step.
notasIA: The first item starts open (`defaultOpen` is 0); pass `defaultOpen={-1}` to start with everything closed.
Items are `{ title, content }`: `title` is plain text and `content` accepts any React node; there is no `value` or `onValueChange`.
Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/accordion/accordion`; it takes 100% of the width, so limit the width on the parent (the demo uses 520 px).

quandoUsar: App navigation with sections and subpages, such as Projects with Assets, Drafts, and Archived, where the group opens in place.
Admin panels that need to collapse the navigation into a 64 px icon rail, with each icon's name in a tooltip.
Navigation with counters on rows (`badge`) and destinations that are real links (`href`).
quandoEvitar: Use `bounce-sidebar` when the destinations are a flat list, without nested groups.
Use `tree-view` or `file-tree` for multi-level content hierarchies; here groups have a single level and children of a child are not drawn.
Use `site-header` for the main navigation of a public site, at the top of the page.

teclado.acao: Moves focus to the next or previous row, including those of open groups, wrapping to the first after the last.
Moves focus to the first or last row.
On a closed group row, opens the group; on the rail, opens the panel and the group together.
On an open group row, closes the group; on a nested row, moves focus to the group row.
Activates the row or opens and closes the group; rows with `href` are links and respond to `Enter`.

acessibilidade: It is a `<nav>` with `aria-label` coming from `label` (default “Sidebar”); each section is a `group` named by its title, and the visual title is hidden from the screen reader.
Group rows are buttons with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; the active leaf gets `aria-current="page"`, and disabled rows use `disabled` or, on links, `aria-disabled` without `href`.
On the rail, the label stays in the DOM with zero opacity and a Radix tooltip appears on hover or focus; the button names “Expand sidebar” and “Collapse sidebar” are fixed in English.
movimento: The width toggles between `width` and `collapsedWidth` on a no-overshoot spring; the icons stay still in a 40 px cell while the panel narrows around them.
A group opens with a height spring and its rows arrive one after another, sliding 8 px from the left; a single highlight slides under the cursor or keyboard focus.
With “reduce motion” on, width, groups, and highlight change instantly and the CSS transitions are turned off.
responsivo: The bar takes `height: 100%` and scrolls inside when the rows do not fit; the parent needs a defined height.
It does not collapse on its own on narrow screens: decide `collapsed` from the window width, as the demo does below 560 px.
notasIA: It needs the `hover-highlight` item installed; import `AnimatedSidebar` from `@/components/ryan-ui/animated-sidebar/animated-sidebar`.
The `id`s must be unique across the whole bar and `value` is always the `id` of a leaf: a row with `children` only opens the group, never navigates.
When controlling `collapsed`, also handle `onCollapsedChange` when a group is opened from the rail: the component asks to expand the panel before showing the children.

quandoUsar: Secondary tasks on mobile where a preview helps before the full view: order summary, sharing options, filters, trip details.
Content that people drag between half height and almost full screen, with rest heights such as `detents={[0.4, 0.85]}`.
Flows that need to know where the sheet stopped, through the index that `onDetentChange` reports.
quandoEvitar: Use `dialog` when the decision needs to interrupt the person in the center of the screen.
Use `drawer` for side panels on wide screens; this sheet is at most 36rem wide and is centered on the bottom edge.

teclado.acao: With focus on the sheet, open to the greatest height; when already open, scroll the content.
With focus on the sheet, scroll the content up.
On the handle, go up or down one rest height; going down it stops at the smallest, without closing.
On the handle, go to the greatest or smallest height.
On the handle, toggle between the smallest and greatest height.
Closes the sheet and returns focus to the `trigger`; while it is open, focus stays trapped in it.

acessibilidade: It is a Radix modal dialog: `title` becomes the accessible name, `description` the description, and the rest of the page leaves the accessibility tree while the sheet is open.
On open, focus goes to the sheet itself; the handle is a button with `aria-expanded` and the label “Expand sheet” or “Collapse sheet”.
Each height change is announced in a polite `aria-live` region (“Sheet expanded”, “Sheet collapsed”); these texts are fixed in English, and only the close button accepts its own label (`closeLabel`).
movimento: The sheet follows the finger 1:1 downward and resists like elastic above the greatest height; on release, velocity projects the destination and a fast gesture always advances at least one height.
A fast downward gesture from the smallest height closes the sheet keeping its velocity; the backdrop darkening follows the position instead of a fixed time.
With “reduce motion” on, the sheet goes straight to each height and only fades on enter and exit; content scrolling is no longer smooth.
responsivo: The width is `min(100%, 36rem)` and the heights are fractions of `100dvh`; the bottom spacing respects the device safe area (`safe-area-inset-bottom`).

The content only scrolls at the greatest height; below it, dragging, spinning the wheel, or tabbing to an off-screen field opens the sheet first, and an observer repositions it when the window height changes.
notasIA: `title` is required and `detents` are fractions of the window height (default `[0.45, 0.92]`), sorted by the component; `initialDetent` is the index in that sorted list.
Pass the button in `trigger` so focus returns to it on close; to close from inside, wrap the action in `BottomSheetClose asChild`.
On touch, dragging vertically over the content moves the sheet until it is fully open; only then does the content scroll. Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/bottom-sheet/bottom-sheet`.

quandoUsar: The main navigation of an app with four to eight flat destinations, where an icon rail frees up width for the content.
Dashboard shells with fixed destinations at the foot of the bar, such as Settings and Help, passed in `secondaryItems`.
Counters that need to stay visible on the rail: the `badge` becomes a dot over the icon.
quandoEvitar: Use `animated-sidebar` when there are nested groups, destinations with `href`, or a need for a tooltip with each icon's name on the rail.
Avoid it with many destinations or little height: the bar does not scroll, and the last rows and the collapse button get cut off.
Use `site-header` for the navigation of a public site.

teclado.acao: Moves focus between the rows and the collapse button, wrapping to the start after the last.
Moves focus to the first row or to the collapse button, which is the last.
Selects the focused row or toggles between rail and panel.

acessibilidade: It is a `<nav>` with `aria-label` coming from `label` (default “Main”); the active row gets `aria-current="page"`.
On the rail, labels and counters stay in the DOM with zero opacity, so the screen reader keeps reading each destination; there is no visual tooltip with the icon's name.
The collapse button has `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` pointing to the bar, and a hidden name “Collapse sidebar” or “Expand sidebar”, fixed in English in the code.
movimento: The width switches between `railWidth` and `panelWidth` on a spring with a small bounce; the active item marker takes the full width and stretches along.
On open, the labels arrive one after another sliding 6 px; on close, they leave together in a 120 ms fade. The marker slides to the active row with a slight bounce.
With “reduce motion” on, width, labels, and marker change instantly, and the icon shrink on press is turned off.
responsivo: The bar has `height: 100%` and does not scroll inside; with little height, the last rows and the collapse button get cut off, so the parent needs enough height.
It does not collapse on its own on narrow screens; the demo starts on the rail below 560 px by passing a controlled `expanded`.
notasIA: The rows are `<button>` without `href`: do the navigation in `onValueChange`, for example by calling the router.
Every item needs a unique `id` and `icon` (about 18 px); `defaultValue` falls back to the first item and `defaultExpanded` starts as `true`.
Import `BounceSidebar` from `@/components/ryan-ui/bounce-sidebar/bounce-sidebar` and put it in a flex row beside the page, with a defined height.

quandoUsar: Frequently asked questions on a landing page where the open item should stand out from the block, with an icon before each question.
Lists where several answers can stay open at the same time, with `multiple`.
Accordions whose state comes from outside, such as the URL or a form, with `value` and `onValueChange`.
quandoEvitar: Use `accordion` on dense pages or documentation, where thin dividers and less motion fit better.
Use `collapsible` for a single region that opens and closes.
Use `faq-section` when you need the whole question section, with topics or search.

teclado.acao: Opens or closes the focused item; without `multiple`, opening one closes the others.
Moves focus to the next or previous title, skipping disabled ones and wrapping to the first after the last.
Moves focus to the first or last enabled title.

acessibilidade: Each title is a `<button>` inside a heading of level `headingLevel` (default 3), with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; the panel is a `region` tied to the title.
When it finishes closing, the panel gets `visibility: hidden` and leaves the Tab order and the accessibility tree; the icon and plus sign are hidden from the screen reader.
Items with `disabled` use the button's native `disabled` and are skipped by the arrows.
movimento: The open item breaks away from its neighbors: the margins grow from 3 px up to `gap` and the corners facing the space round up to `radius`, on a spring with a small bounce.
The height opens with the same bounce and closes on a no-overshoot spring; the content moves down 10 px as it appears and the plus sign rotates 135° until it becomes an x.
With “reduce motion” on, margins, corners, height, and icon change instantly, and the button's grow on hover is turned off.
notasIA: `value` is always a list of strings, even without `multiple`, and `onValueChange` receives the whole list; all start closed (`defaultValue` is `[]`).
When turning off `multiple` with controlled state, trim the list yourself, as the demo does with `current.slice(-1)`; the component does not do this.
Each item needs a unique `value`; `title` accepts any React node and `icon` is optional. Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/bouncy-accordion/bouncy-accordion`.

quandoUsar: Deep pages in a hierarchy, such as Workspace › Projects › Mobile app › Releases, so people can go back to any level.
Folder or category browsers where the path lives in local state: items with `onClick` and no `href` become buttons.
Paths that grow as the person descends the tree: new levels slide in at the end.
quandoEvitar: Use `stepper` to show the progress of a multi-step flow; the trail shows location, not progress.
Use `tabs` to switch between sibling views at the same level.
Use `pagination` to move through the pages of a collection.
acessibilidade: Renders a `<nav>` with `aria-label` (default “Breadcrumb”, in English) and an ordered list; the arrows between levels are hidden from the screen reader.
The last item is always the current page: it becomes text with `aria-current="page"`, even if it has `href`.
movimento: Items from the first render stay still; levels added later slide in 8 px from the left, out of a slight blur, and removed ones disappear in a short fade.
The items that remain reposition on a no-overshoot spring, and each reserves the label width at medium weight, so becoming the current page does not shift the path.
With “reduce motion” on, entries, exits, and repositioning happen instantly.
responsivo: The list wraps onto several lines when it does not fit (`flex-wrap`), but each label stays on a single line; there is no ellipsis or collapsing of the middle levels.
notasIA: Pass the whole path in `items`, with the current page last; use `href` for real routes and `onClick` without `href` for paths in local state.
Links go through `RyanProvider`: with it, `next/link` or your router's Link is used in place of the `<a>`.
Change `ariaLabel` to Portuguese, for example “Trilha de navegação”, since the default is “Breadcrumb”. Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/breadcrumb/breadcrumb`.

quandoUsar: Galleries of templates, recipes, or integrations where each card opens its own details without changing pages.
Catalogs where the card summary (`summary`) is enough to choose and the full content (`content`) only appears in the modal, with actions in the footer.
Grids where continuity matters: icon and title travel from the card to the modal header.
quandoEvitar: Use `dialog` for a confirmation or form that does not originate from a card in a grid.
Use `expandable-card` when the details fit in the card itself and the page does not need to be blocked.
Use `image-viewer` for photo galleries with zoom and navigation between images.

teclado.acao: On the focused card, opens the modal.
Move through the modal controls without leaving it; on open, focus goes to the first control, the close button.
Closes the modal; focus returns to the card that opened it.

acessibilidade: Each card is a `<button>` with `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded`; the modal is a Radix dialog with the title as its name and the `subtitle` as its description.
With the modal open, focus is trapped in it and the rest of the page leaves the accessibility tree; on close, focus returns to the originating card.
The close button is named “Close”, fixed in English in the code; the card media is hidden from the screen reader.
movimento: The card's box, media, and title are the same elements as the modal's and travel to the center on a spring with a slight bounce; on close, they return on a spring without bounce.
The summary disappears while subtitle, body, and footer arrive one after another, rising 12 px out of a slight blur, and all leave at once.
With “reduce motion” on, there is no shared travel: the modal only fades on enter and exit.
responsivo: The grid uses `auto-fill` with columns of at least `minColumnWidth` (default 220 px) and loses columns as the width shrinks.
The modal takes the screen width minus 2rem up to `width` (default 480 px), with a maximum height of `100dvh` minus 2rem and inner scrolling.
notasIA: Each item has `id`, `title`, and `content`; `summary` and `meta` only appear on the card, and `subtitle` and `media` appear on both.
Use `renderFooter(item, close)` for the actions and call `close()` after acting; to control the open card, use `value` (an `id` or `null`) with `onValueChange`.
Import `CenterMorphModal` from `@/components/ryan-ui/center-morph-modal/center-morph-modal`; it draws the whole grid, so pass all the cards at once.

quandoUsar: Advanced settings beside a title, such as build options, with a summary in `hint` that changes with the state.
“Show more” below a short list, with the `plain` variant and the trigger placed after the content.
Forms with an optional block: the content stays mounted when closed, so the fields keep their value.
quandoEvitar: Use `accordion` for a set of related sections where only one is open at a time.
Use `expandable-text` for a long paragraph clipped to a few lines.
Use `popover` when the detail should float over the page instead of pushing the content below.

teclado.acao: On the trigger, opens or closes the region.

acessibilidade: The trigger is a `<button>` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; the content is a `region` named by the trigger.
After closing, the region gets `visibility: hidden` and leaves the Tab order and the accessibility tree, although it stays mounted.
With `disabled` on the `Collapsible`, the trigger is disabled and the current state is kept; icon and arrow are hidden from the screen reader.
movimento: The height follows the content on a no-overshoot spring, and the content rises 8 px out of a 4 px blur as it appears.
The arrow rotates 180° on a short spring; a new click mid-animation reverses the motion from where it is.
With “reduce motion” on, the region opens and closes instantly and the color and border transitions are turned off.
desempenho: The content stays mounted even when closed, so it is rendered from the start; on a page with many `Collapsible`s with heavy content, all of that content exists at the same time.
notasIA: Assemble the three parts: `Collapsible` on the outside, `CollapsibleTrigger` and `CollapsibleContent` inside; outside a `Collapsible`, the parts throw an error.
To control it, pass `open` with `onOpenChange`; an `onClick` on the trigger that calls `preventDefault()` cancels the toggle.
`variant="card"` (default) draws a bordered surface; `plain` leaves trigger and content without a frame. Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/collapsible/collapsible`.

quandoUsar: Confirming a destructive action, such as deleting a project, explaining the consequences in `description`.
A short form that must be completed or canceled before returning to the page.
Decisions that cannot go unnoticed: the backdrop darkens with a blur and the page behind becomes inaccessible until the dialog closes.
quandoEvitar: Use `drawer` for longer tasks where people still want to see the page beside it.
Use `popover` for contextual information that does not need to block the page.
Use `confirm-morph` or `hold-to-confirm` to confirm a destructive action on the button itself, without opening a window.

teclado.acao: Move through the dialog controls without leaving it; on open, focus goes to the first control, the close button.
Closes the dialog and returns focus to the `DialogTrigger`.

acessibilidade: Radix modal dialog: `role="dialog"` with `title` as its name (an `<h2>`) and `description` as its description; the rest of the page leaves the accessibility tree and scrolling is locked.
Focus is trapped in the dialog and returns to the trigger on close; the close button is named “Close dialog”, fixed in English in the code.
To send initial focus to another control, use `onOpenAutoFocus` on `DialogContent`, which forwards the Radix props.
movimento: The backdrop fades in with a 7 px blur while the panel rises 8 px and grows from 96% on a no-overshoot spring; closing is shorter and starts from wherever the entrance is.
If `title` or `description` change while the dialog is open, the new text rises and the old one exits upward.
With “reduce motion” on, backdrop and panel only fade, in 120 ms.
responsivo: The panel is up to 440 px wide (the screen minus 2rem on phones) with a maximum height of `100dvh` minus 2rem, scrolling inside when the content exceeds that.
notasIA: Assemble `Dialog`, `DialogTrigger asChild` around the button, and `DialogContent` with `title`; buttons that close go in `DialogClose asChild`. Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/dialog/dialog`.
To close after an async action, control it with `open` and `onOpenChange` and pass `false` when it finishes, as the demo does.
Use this file's `Dialog` as the root: under a plain Radix `Root`, `DialogContent` animates with CSS keyframes, without the Motion spring.

quandoUsar: Editing a record or profile without losing the list view, with the form in a side panel.
List filters opened from the left (`side="left"`) and applied on close.
Details of a selected row that stay on screen while the panel leaves, with `useDrawerItem`.
quandoEvitar: Use `dialog` for a short decision that needs full attention.
Use `bottom-sheet` on mobile when the panel should rest at different heights and follow the finger.
Use `resizable-panels` when the side panel is a permanent part of the layout.

teclado.acao: Move through the panel controls without leaving it; on open, focus goes to the first control, the close button.
Closes the panel and returns focus to the `DrawerTrigger`.

acessibilidade: It is a Radix modal dialog: `title` gives the name, `description` the description, focus is trapped in the panel, and the rest of the page leaves the accessibility tree.
The close button is named “Close drawer”, fixed in English in the code.
movimento: The panel enters from the `side` edge on a no-overshoot spring and leaves faster, fading only in the last stretch so the shadow does not vanish abruptly.
The header is the handle: dragging toward the edge moves the panel, the other side resists like elastic, and passing a third of the panel or making a fast gesture closes it keeping the velocity.
With “reduce motion” on, there is no drag and the panel only fades on enter and exit.
responsivo: On the sides the panel is up to 30rem and, below 40rem, takes almost the full width, with smaller corners and spacing; at the top or bottom it takes the full width, up to 32rem tall.
With `container`, the panel opens inside an element, anchored to its edges; that element needs `position: relative` and `overflow: hidden`.
notasIA: Assemble `Drawer`, `DrawerTrigger asChild`, and `DrawerContent` with `title` and `side`; actions that close go in `DrawerClose asChild`. Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/drawer/drawer`.
When opening from a selected row, pass the item through `useDrawerItem(item)` and render the result, so the content does not vanish while the panel leaves.
Drag-to-close only exists with this file's `Drawer` root; under a plain Radix `Root`, the panel animates with CSS keyframes and does not drag.

quandoUsar: Event or meeting cards that show a title and time and reveal agenda and attendees on request.
Dense summaries in a dashboard that can also grow sideways when opened, with `width` and `expandedWidth`.
Cards whose supporting line changes over time: only the new words of `description` animate.
quandoEvitar: Use `collapsible` when the open state needs to be controlled from outside; this card only accepts `defaultExpanded`.
Use `center-morph-modal` when the details are long and deserve a focused window.
Use `accordion` for a list of sections where only one is open at a time.

teclado.acao: On the header, opens or closes the card.
With the card open and focus inside it, closes it and returns focus to the header.

acessibilidade: The header is a `<button>` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; when closed, the panel is `inert`, out of focus and out of the screen reader.
The animated `description` has a hidden copy for the screen reader, which reads the whole sentence instead of loose words.
movimento: Width and height grow on the same no-overshoot spring, with real size instead of scale, so text, border, and corners do not stretch.
On close, the details fade first and the box shrinks 60 ms later; on open, they appear once the box has made room, and the arrow rotates 180°.
With “reduce motion” on, the card opens and closes instantly.
responsivo: An observer measures the available width: the card stays centered, never exceeds the container, and `width` and `expandedWidth` work only as limits.
notasIA: There is no `expanded` or `onExpandedChange`: the state is internal and starts from `defaultExpanded`.
Without `width`, the card fills the container; for it to grow sideways on open, pass both limits, such as `width={360}` and `expandedWidth={460}`.
`title` and `description` are text; the details go in `children`. Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/expandable-card/expandable-card`.

quandoUsar: Long product descriptions, bios, or reviews in a list, clipped to a few lines with `lines`.
Variable-length texts where the button should only appear when the text actually exceeds the clip.
Paragraphs with links in the middle: the whole text stays in the DOM, and a link hidden below the clip opens the text when it receives focus.
quandoEvitar: Use `collapsible` when the hidden part is a separate block, such as a list or a form, and not the continuation of the text.
Use `accordion` for several sections with their own titles.

teclado.acao: On the button, opens or closes the text.
When focus reaches a link hidden below the clip, the text opens on its own.

acessibilidade: The button has `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; the two labels share the same space and the inactive one is hidden, so the name read is always the current one.
The clipped text stays whole in the DOM, available to the screen reader; the clip is only visual.
movimento: The height slides with a smooth deceleration, 500 to 600 ms on open and 400 to 450 ms on close, depending on the distance; the fade on the last line goes away along with it and the arrow rotates in step.
When closing with the start of the text off screen, the page scrolls back to it.
With “reduce motion” on, the text opens and closes instantly, the labels swap without a transition, and the scroll back is instant.
responsivo: At rest, the clip is CSS in `lh`, and an observer remeasures when the width or font changes: the button appears or disappears depending on whether the text exceeds the clip.
desempenho: Each instance uses a `ResizeObserver` to know whether the text overflows; in a long list, that is one observer per item.
notasIA: Translate the labels with `moreLabel` and `lessLabel`; the defaults are “Read more” and “Show less”.
Do not draw your own “read more”: the button already appears only when the text exceeds `lines` lines (default 3).
To control it, pass `expanded` with `onExpandedChange`. Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/expandable-text/expandable-text`.

quandoUsar: Mentions of people in a text, such as authors and reviewers, with `HoverCardProfile` showing photo, role, bio, and numbers.
Avatars or names in a list where the click should stay free to open the profile.
Previews of links or references that help decide before leaving the page.
quandoEvitar: Use `tooltip` for a short text that names or explains a control.
Use `popover` when the content has buttons, links, or fields: the card does not receive focus, so nothing inside it is reachable by keyboard.
Use `citations` for numbered sources inside an AI response.

teclado.acao: When the trigger is focused by keyboard, the card opens right away; when leaving the trigger, it closes.
Closes the card; it only reopens after focus or the pointer leaves the trigger and comes back.

acessibilidade: The card has `role="tooltip"` and, when open, the trigger gets `aria-describedby` pointing to it: the screen reader reads the content as the trigger's description.
Focus never enters the card; keep the content read-only and leave any action on the trigger itself.
On touch, a tap on the trigger opens and closes the card; the profile photo has an empty `alt`, because the name is already in the text.
movimento: The first card waits `openDelay` (500 ms); with another one open recently, the next opens in 80 ms and only fades.
The card grows from the trigger edge: it starts at 96% and 4 px toward the trigger on a no-overshoot spring, and returns from wherever it is if the pointer comes back during the exit.
With “reduce motion” on, the card only fades, the profile rows do not enter in sequence, and the photo does not come out of a blur.
responsivo: The width is 18.5rem, shrinking to the available width, and the card switches sides when it does not fit, with 12 px of clearance from the edge.
notasIA: The child is the trigger and must accept `ref` and receive focus, like a `<button>` or a link; the preview goes in `content`.
Only one card is open at a time across the whole page; there is no need to coordinate the instances.
`HoverCardProfile` accepts `avatar` as a URL or as an element (for example `next/image`) and shows initials without a photo. Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/hover-card/hover-card`.

quandoUsar: A create button, such as “New project”, that opens a short form coming out of the button itself.
Sharing or inviting from a toolbar button, with the list of people in the modal body.
Primary actions where the origin of the modal must be clear: the panel is born from the position, size, and color of the button.
quandoEvitar: Use `dialog` when the modal is opened by code, by a menu item, or by more than one trigger; here the trigger is always the component's own button.
Use `center-morph-modal` when the modals originate from cards in a grid.
Use `popover` for small content that does not need to block the page.

teclado.acao: On the button, opens the modal.
Move through the modal controls without leaving it; on open, focus goes to the first form field or, with no fields, to the close button.
Closes the modal, which turns back into the button, and returns focus to it.

acessibilidade: The button gets `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded`; the panel is a Radix modal dialog with `title` as its name and `description` as its description.
To choose the initial focus, mark the element with `data-autofocus`; the close button is named “Close”, fixed in English in the code.
movimento: The panel grows from the button's box on a spring with a slight bounce and returns to it on an exact spring, without oscillating; it starts at the button color and lightens to the surface color.
Title, body, and footer arrive one after another, rising 10 px out of a slight blur, and leave all at once so they do not follow the shrinking.
With “reduce motion” on, there is no transformation: the panel only fades on open and close.
responsivo: The panel takes the screen width minus 2rem up to `width` (default 420 px), with a maximum height of `100dvh` minus 2rem and inner scrolling.
notasIA: `trigger` is the button's content (label and icon), not a button: the component draws its own `<button>`; style it with `variant` and `triggerClassName`.
`children` and `footer` accept a function that receives `{ close }`, useful for closing after saving.
Control it with `open` and `onOpenChange` when needed; import `MorphingModal` from `@/components/ryan-ui/morphing-modal/morphing-modal`.

quandoUsar: A small panel next to a button, such as the share link with a copy action.
Quick settings or filters that people open, change, and close without leaving context.
Contextual information with one or two controls, which should not block the rest of the page.
quandoEvitar: Use `tooltip` for a short, non-interactive text that names a control.
Use `dropdown-menu` for a list of actions.
Use `dialog` when the decision needs to block the page until it is made.

teclado.acao: On the trigger, open or close the panel; on open, focus goes to the first control inside.
Cycle through the panel controls.
Closes the panel and returns focus to the trigger.

acessibilidade: It is the non-modal Radix Popover: the trigger gets `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded`, and `aria-controls`, and the panel has `role="dialog"`.
The panel has no accessible name by default; pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` to `PopoverContent`.
The page behind stays accessible and scrollable; clicking outside or moving focus outside closes the panel.
movimento: The panel starts a few pixels toward the trigger, at 97% size, and settles with a CSS spring curve; it leaves faster than it enters.
These are transitions, not keyframes: closing mid-open, or reopening during the close, reverses from wherever the panel is.
With “reduce motion” on, the panel only fades.
responsivo: The width goes from 12rem to `min(22rem, 100vw - 20px)`, and the panel switches sides when it does not fit, with 10 px of clearance from the edge (`collisionPadding`).
notasIA: Assemble `Popover`, `PopoverTrigger asChild` around the button, and `PopoverContent`; actions that close go in `PopoverClose asChild`.
The defaults are `align="start"` and `sideOffset={6}`; `side` and the other Radix props pass straight through to `PopoverContent`.
Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/popover/popover`; `PopoverContent` already comes in a portal, with 1rem of inner padding, so do not wrap the content in another card.

quandoUsar: Email or editor layouts, such as folders, list, and reading side by side, where each person adjusts the space for the task.
A side panel that can be hidden by dragging it to the edge (`collapsible`) and comes back through the tab that appears on the divider.
Comparing two pieces of content side by side, such as code and preview, with limits in px (`minSize`, `maxSize`).
quandoEvitar: Use `image-compare` to compare two overlaid images with a divider.
Use `drawer` or `tabs` on phone screens, where side-by-side panels become too narrow.
Avoid it when you need a vertical split, with one panel above the other: the group only splits horizontally.

teclado.acao: On the focused divider, move the edge 16 px; at the limit of a collapsible panel, the next arrow hides it and the opposite one brings it back at the minimum.
Move the edge 64 px.
Take the left panel to the smallest or largest allowed size.
Hides the neighboring collapsible panel or shows the hidden one again.
During a drag, returns the divider to the position it started from.

acessibilidade: Each divider is a focusable `separator` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, and `aria-valuemax` in percent, named by the `label` of the panel on the left and tied to it by `aria-controls`.
With a panel hidden, the divider announces “<name> hidden, press Enter to show”, fixed text in English, and the hidden content is `inert`.
The group is a `group` named by `label`; `aria-valuenow` already shows the destination as soon as the spring starts, without waiting for it to settle.
movimento: The divider follows the pointer 1:1 and resists like elastic past the limits; pulling well below the minimum of a `collapsible` panel, or making a fast gesture toward the edge, closes it.
State changes and the keyboard use no-overshoot springs; the content fades as the panel is squeezed below the minimum and stays pinned to the moving edge, like a drawer.
With “reduce motion” on, the panels go straight to the final size and the restore tab only fades.
responsivo: The group is a size container: when it gets narrower than the sum of the minimums, each minimum shrinks proportionally, and the panels keep their proportions when the window changes.
The group takes `height: 100%`, so the parent needs a defined height; the demo uses a 260 px box.
notasIA: Assemble `ResizablePanels` with `ResizablePanel` children, each with a unique `id`, `label`, and `defaultSize` (relative proportions, they do not need to add up to 100); `minSize` is in px and defaults to 80.
The set of panels must stay the same for the whole life of the group; to swap the panels, remount the group with a different `key`.
To remember the layout, save the percentages from `onLayoutChange` and pass them as `defaultSize` on the next mount; a double click on the divider returns to the default.

quandoUsar: Height-limited lists inside cards, menus, or panels, with `maxHeight`, where thick native bars would be heavy.
Horizontal strips of chips or filters (`orientation="horizontal"`), where the vertical mouse wheel scrolls sideways while there is room.
Strips with native snapping via `snap`, without replacing system scrolling with a simulated one.
quandoEvitar: Use `message-scroller` for conversations that need to follow new messages.
Use `carousel` when the strip needs arrows, indicators, and an active slide.
For scrolling the whole page, let the browser scroll; the area is meant for inner regions.

teclado.acao: Scroll the content on the axes that scroll, when the area is focused; the scrolling is the browser's native one.
Scroll one page at a time.

acessibilidade: The scroll viewport always enters the Tab order; with `label`, it becomes a named `region`, so always pass a `label` so it is not an unnamed focus stop.
The drawn bars are hidden from the screen reader; scrolling stays native, so keyboard, touch, and assistive technologies work as on the platform.
movimento: The bars appear on scroll or pointer hover and fade out after `hideDelay` (900 ms); the thumb thickens under the cursor.
Each edge fades only when there is content beyond it, growing over the first pixels of scroll up to `fade` px (default 28; 0 turns it off).
Clicking the track scrolls 90% of the visible area with a smooth animation, which becomes a jump with “reduce motion” on; the bar transitions are also turned off.
responsivo: On touch screens, without a hovering pointer, the bars only appear during scrolling; `scrollbars="always"` keeps them visible when there is overflow.
The area only scrolls with a limited height: pass `maxHeight` or give the parent a height.
desempenho: Scrolling does not re-render React: bars and fades are written straight to the DOM, and a `ResizeObserver` together with a `MutationObserver` tracks changes in the content.
notasIA: Import `ScrollArea` from `@/components/ryan-ui/scroll-area/scroll-area`; `orientation` accepts `vertical` (default), `horizontal`, and `both`.
Use `onEdgeChange` to know when the end has been reached, for example to load more, and `viewportRef` to scroll from code.
With `snap`, set `scroll-snap-align` on the children; the component only forwards the value to the viewport's `scroll-snap-type`.

quandoUsar: Related views of the same object, such as Overview, Activity, Members, and Billing of a project.
Settings sections where people look at one at a time and the rest of the page stays the same.
Many tabs in a narrow space: the list scrolls sideways, with fading at the edges and scroll buttons.
quandoEvitar: Use `segmented-control` when the switch is a mode or filter without its own content panel.
Use `accordion` when people need to read several sections in sequence, as on a long page on a phone.
Use `stepper` for steps in order that people go through once.

teclado.acao: Enters the list at the active tab and, from there, goes to the panel.
Move focus to the previous or next tab and activate it right away, wrapping to the first after the last.
Go to the first or last tab.
Activate the focused tab.

acessibilidade: Built on the Radix Tabs: `tablist`, tabs with `aria-selected` and `aria-controls`, `tabpanel` panels that are focusable and tied to the tab, and a roving `tabindex` for focus.
Pass `aria-label` to `TabsList` to name the set; the scroll buttons are named “Scroll tabs left” and “Scroll tabs right”, fixed in English in the code.
The panel that leaves is `inert` while it fades, receiving neither clicks nor focus.
movimento: The active tab's highlight slides to the new tab on a no-overshoot spring, always within the same `Tabs`.
The new panel enters 8 px from the side of the chosen tab, the old one leaves quickly toward the other side, and the height goes from the previous to the new on a no-overshoot spring.
With “reduce motion” on, the highlight jumps, the panels only fade in place, the height does not animate, and the list scrolling is instant.
responsivo: When the tabs do not fit, the list scrolls sideways with fading at the edges and arrow buttons, and the active or focused tab is brought into view.
notasIA: Pass `defaultValue`, or `value` with `onValueChange`; without them no tab starts selected and no panel appears.
Inactive panels are unmounted and lose their internal state; with `forceMount` they stay mounted, but also visible, so hide the inactive one through `data-state="inactive"`.
Assemble `Tabs`, `TabsList` with one `TabsTrigger` per tab, and a `TabsContent` with the same `value` as each tab. Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/tabs/tabs`.

quandoUsar: Naming icon-only buttons in a toolbar, such as Bold, Italic, and Link.
Showing a control's keyboard shortcut, such as “Bold (Ctrl+B)”.
A short explanation for an unfamiliar control; if the text changes while the bubble is open, such as “Copy” to “Copied”, the swap is animated.
quandoEvitar: Use `hover-card` for rich previews of a person or a link.
Use `popover` when the content has buttons, links, or fields.
Avoid it for essential information: on touch the tooltip does not open, so it should be visible on screen.

teclado.acao: When the trigger is focused by keyboard, the tooltip appears; when leaving, it disappears.
Closes the tooltip without taking focus off the trigger.

acessibilidade: The bubble has `role="tooltip"` and, when open, the trigger gets `aria-describedby` pointing to it: the text is a description, not the control's name.
On an icon-only button, pass `aria-label` on the button itself; the tooltip complements it, as in the demo.
Radix ignores touch pointers and does not open the tooltip on focus caused by touch or click, so it does not appear on phones.
movimento: The first tooltip waits 250 ms and slides 3 px from the trigger, growing from 97%; while any is open, and for up to 300 ms after, the next opens instantly and only fades.
When a text `content` changes with the bubble open, the new one rises, the old one exits upward, and the bubble adjusts its size on a spring.
With “reduce motion” on, the bubble only fades and the text swap happens without displacement.
responsivo: The bubble is up to 15rem wide and wraps the text into lines; it switches sides when it does not fit, with 12 px of clearance from the edge.
notasIA: The child must be a single element that accepts `ref` and receives focus, such as a `<button>`; the text goes in `content`.
There is only `content`, `children`, and `side` (default `top`); the delay and the quick-switch window are fixed in the code.
Each `Tooltip` brings its own Radix provider, so there is no need to wrap the app in a `TooltipProvider`. Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/tooltip/tooltip`.
